answer_1.quote: We propose a novel method Contrastive Attributed explanations for Text (CAT) which provides contrastive explanations for natural language data... Our method produces fluent contrasts... We adopt a different strategy where we first take the original sentence... An MLM pre‑trained BERT model is then used to fill these masks.

answer_2.quote: For each dataset, we measure the following properties: i) Flip rate (Flip), ii) Edit distance (Dist), iii) Content Preservation (Cont), and iv) Fluency... We report means of each metric across all instances obtained from generated contrastive sentences.
automatic_metrics: Content preservation (cosine similarity of sentence embeddings)

answer_4.quote: We now describe two user studies we conducted to ascertain the value of our attributed explanations... A total of 75 participants with backgrounds in data science, engineering and business analytics voluntarily took part in user studies... participants were asked to assess explanations along four dimensions: completeness, sufficiency, satisfaction and understandability using a 5‑point Likert scale.
answer_4.guideline: Participants answered Likert‑scale questions on completeness, sufficiency, satisfaction, and understandability for each explanation method.
